newsitem.title: USA: Delta's pay raise for workers a good investment.
newsitem.headline: Delta's pay raise for workers a good investment.

text.p: Even though Wall Street took a bit off the top of Delta's stock on Thursday after it announced a $137 million pay raise for non-union employees, the move is likely to help the carrier in the long run.

Delta Air Lines Inc's stock took off to a new high of 94-3/4 amid strength in the airline industry, but after the announcement of the wage hike, it settled back to 92-3/8, closing up 1-1/2 to 92-3/8 on the New York Stock Exchange.

"That's a knee-jerk reaction by traders, especially in a market as touchy as this one, who are likely to think the company is giving away the store. But its far from the truth," said Joseph De Blasi, a professor at Rutgers University's School of Management and Labor Relations.

The raise should calm concerns of non-union employees who have seen their union counterparts win pacts with stock ownership, options and some with pay increases at Delta and UAL Corp's United Airlines, analysts said. AMR Corp's American Airlines currently has a similar tentative contract which pilots are expected to approve.
That means non-union employees should be less likely to unionize despite their lower salary packages, analysts said. It would also keep morale up for the employees who directly deal with customers.
The recent bonanza in earnings in the airline industry mean more salary hikes by other U.S. carriers are on the horizon, analysts said.

"(Continental) is clearly ready to improve the income potential of their employees, many of whom have been through the worst of times with the company," said Dillon Read & Co Inc airline analyst Edward Starkman.
Another analyst, who declined to be identified, said United is likely to announce a pay raise for non-union workers and that is highly likely that AMR is in similar talks.

Delta Air Lines Inc said it will lift the salaries of mechanics, flight attendants, and ticket agents by up to five percent, restore certain vacation benefits, and boost profit-sharing from five to six percent.
"Our commitment ... is to provide Delta people with the opportunity to be at the top of our industry in total compensation," said Delta chairman Ronald Allen in a memo to employees.
One Wall Street airline analyst, who declined to be identified, said the raise might raise the eyebrows of union workers at Delta.

Pilots at Delta took a two percent pay cut in return for stock options and a profit-sharing plan comparable to those enjoyed by other Delta employees. They also received a seat on the company's board and improved retirement benefits.

Karen McGuffy, a spokeswoman for the Air Line Pilots' Association said, "We are very pleased that management has recognized the contributions of the non-contract employees to the company's record setting financial performance, and believe the pilot's group significant contribution must be addressed as well."
Delta Air Lines said it could not specify how many employees would be affected by the raise package.
Neither Continental Airlines Inc nor United Airlines could be reached for comment.
Airline stocks closed sharply higher on Thursday after AMR and Continental posted stronger than expected quarterly earnings and the favorable downturn in interest rates.
AMR shares jumped 2-1/2 to 87-1/2, UAL shares gained 1-5/8 to 74-5/8 and Continental added 1/8 to 32-1/2.
